senses.gloss:
yuktyābhāsa
(‘semblance of reason’)
------------------------------------------
In the Indian philosophical treatises, a quotation from a standard text is taken up for discussion. A सṁशय or doubt is raised about its correct meaning by mentioning two or more alternatives. The opponent (called pūrvapakṣin) supports one of the views and gives his yuktis or arguments. The siddhāntin (propounder of the correct theory) refutes these arguments by showing that they are only a semblance of arguments and not true. This is termed युक्त्याभास. The arguments of the siddhāntin are called sadyukti or valid reason.
